name: Green-veg & chicken glass-noodle stir-fry — soy-free (clean sauce)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (screenshot), adapted to the user's real batches
source.notes: Soy-FREE ('clean sauce') green stir-fry — the user's adopted rotation main. Veg is flexible (whatever's on hand). Updated 2026-08-22 to the user's actual logged batch: 630 g chicken, 150 g dry glass noodles, 200 g broccoli, 2 zucchini, 100 g spinach, 8 mushrooms, ½ onion, 8 garlic. No oil/sauce amounts were given for this batch — assumed ~1 tbsp sesame + ~1 tbsp frying oil and light salt/pepper + lemon. Each extra tbsp of oil ≈ +120 kcal / +14 g fat; tell me the real oil and I'll adjust.

serving_desc: ≈410 g cooked (batch ÷4). Logged batch: 630 g raw chicken + 150 g dry glass noodles

logged_instance.veg: 200 g broccoli, 2 zucchini, 100 g spinach, 8 mushrooms, ½ onion, 8 garlic
logged_instance.note: Made with mushrooms + onion in place of the original green beans / green onion / chili.

steps: Sear chicken; stir-fry veg + noodles; fold spinach in at the end; finish with lemon.

batch_totals.note: Sodium low as cooked (no soy) — rises with any added salt/soy.

him.verdict: Your best everyday cutting main. 40.5 g protein for ~443 kcal (~9 g protein per 100 kcal), lean, big green-veg volume, ~4 g fiber, and low sodium because there's no soy. Broccoli + spinach bring folate/vitamin C, mushrooms add selenium (a sperm micro). The only fat lever is the oil (~11 g/serving from sesame + frying oil) — trim it if you want it leaner. Glass noodles are the one refined carb, well balanced.
flags: fat driven by oil — the only lever
suggested_mods: Measure/limit the oil — each tbsp is ~120 kcal; ~1 tbsp total is plenty in a nonstick
Season with lemon, chili, garlic instead of soy to keep sodium low

her_preconception.verdict: The best preconception main in the rotation. Spinach + broccoli make it a real FOLATE dish (~65 mcg DFE/serving, the #1 preconception nutrient), with iron (~2.7 mg) paired with the veg's vitamin C for absorption, plus choline and selenium on lean protein. Fully cooked, no sprouts, no high-mercury fish, low sodium — no safety flags. This is the one to make for her.
prenatal_highlights: folate from spinach + broccoli (~65 mcg DFE/serving) — top preconception nutrient
iron (~2.7 mg) paired with vitamin C for absorption
choline + selenium; lean protein; low sodium
suggested_mods: Fold the spinach in at the very end so the folate isn't cooked out
Keep it lightly seasoned to hold the sodium down

adopted_note: Adopted rotation main (best-scoring + best preconception dish). Veg-flexible — make it with whatever green veg is on hand. Current logged batch (2026-08-22): 630 g chicken / 150 g dry glass noodles / broccoli + zucchini + spinach + mushroom + onion → ~443 kcal, 40.5 g protein per ~410 g serving (batch ÷4). Scales with chicken weight.
cooking_guide: Prep everything first — stir-fry moves fast. Soak the glass noodles in warm water until pliable (5-10 min), drain, and snip shorter with scissors.
Steam or blanch the broccoli ~2 min (it's the densest veg), then drain — this cooks it evenly and keeps it bright and crisp-tender.
Pat the chicken strips dry and season lightly. Heat the pan/wok hot before the oil goes in — high heat sears, low heat steams.
Stir-fry the chicken in a single layer until just cooked, then remove (crowding makes it grey and watery).
Stir-fry the garlic and onion briefly, then the mushrooms — leave the mushrooms undisturbed ~1 min to brown (moving them too soon makes them release water and steam).
Add the zucchini and blanched broccoli and toss 2-3 min to keep them crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, add the noodles with a splash of water and the sesame oil; season to taste (salt, pepper) and toss 1-2 min to combine and heat through.
Fold in the spinach at the very end and toss just until wilted — seconds only; overcooking dulls it and loses folate.
Finish off the heat with a squeeze of lemon or lime — it brightens everything and boosts iron absorption. Serve promptly.
